messages:
Alex W: Heads-up — saw several pods from customer-tenant-b jump onto hosted-gpu-pool in us-west at 04:12 UTC and they pushed the pool to 95% GPU utilization. Dedicated pools for that tenant were idle. Any idea why the scheduler fell back to hosted?
Maria S: hmm that's the fallthrough behavior from our scale-down policy when dedicated nodes aren't Ready/Allocatable. Did the dedicated pool have taints or quota mismatches?
Jamal R: I checked quick logs — dedicated pool had 2 nodes in NotReady for ~7m (kernel OOM killer + node reboot). CA marked nodes as unready, but pods were evicted and rescheduled to other pools.
Tiffany: Are those pods tolerant to hosted pools? They have tolerations for `gpu:exposed` which the hosted pool sets. But we should avoid cross-tenant spillover.
Priya: Right, current policy intentionally allows cross-pool scheduling if no anti-affinity exists. That was to maximize throughput. But customer isolation complains.
Alex W: We need a short-term mitigation + a longer policy decision. Short term: can we enforce nodeAffinity to prefer dedicated first and set `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` awareness?
Maria S: Short-term patch: add `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` + a hard `nodeSelector` fallback only for high-SLA pods. Example snippet: ```yaml
nodeAffinity:
  preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
  - weight: 100
    preference:
      matchExpressions:
      - key: dedicated-pool
        operator: In
        values: ["tenant-b"]
  requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    nodeSelectorTerms:
    - matchExpressions:
      - key: scheduling-strict
        operator: NotIn
        values: ["avoid-hosted-fallback"]
```
Jamal R: That weird `scheduling-strict` trick will prevent fallback onto nodes that we label `avoid-hosted-fallback`. But we'll need an admission mutating webhook to inject those labels / nodeSelector on tenant pods.
Tiffany: We already have a lightweight mutating webhook for sidecar injection. Could repurpose that to add `nodeAffinity` for dedicated-bound workloads. Low effort.
Priya: For longer term, we should update cluster-autoscaler config: prioritize scaling dedicated pools before allowing expansion of hosted pools for tenant-tagged requests. CA has node group priorities but we might need multiple CA instances or CA multi-profile.
Alex W: Agree. Also cost angle: hosted GPUs are cheaper for burst, but if tenants consistently spill over we lose isolation guarantees and can be billing surprise. We need a policy matrix: isolation vs cost tradeoff per customer tier.
Maria S: Proposal: 3-tier behavior — Strict (no fallback), Preferred (prefer dedicated, allow fallback after X minutes), Best-effort (fallback immediately). Default to Preferred for enterprise tier.
Jamal R: Implementation details: add an annotation `redwood.io/scale-fallback: strict|preferred|best-effort` on tenant namespaces. CA + scheduler webhook consult this. For strict, we inject `nodeAffinity` + PodDisruptionBudget tuning so pods don't move.
Priya: We should also add metric alerts: when hosted-pool receives >20% tenant-dedicated traffic for >5m, page infra-oncall. That will surface silent spillovers.
Tiffany: One caution: strict mode can create cold-start failure if dedicated pool can't recover quickly. We need automatic emergency burst where dedicated pool borrows from a shared burst pool that is still tagged as 'private-burst' but isolated network-wise.
Alex W: Good point. Network constraints: hosted pools cross-tenant traffic must NOT be able to access tenant VPCs. Verify our CNI and network policies prevent lateral movement. ops-bot, can you run a quick check?
ops-bot: Scanning networking rules for hosted-gpu-pool in us-west... found 2 namespaces missing netpol deny-egress to tenant VPCs. Reporting to #security.
Maria S: Ok, that's the high priority fix — patch network policies first. Then rollout the mutating webhook to inject nodeAffinity. Then CA config change and annotation rollout.
Jamal R: I'll draft the CA change: set `scaleDownDelayAfterAdd=10m` and `balance-similar-node-groups=true`, plus node group priorities so dedicated groups appear before hosted.
Priya: And add a small quota/burst budget resource in Dedicated pool: reserve 10% headroom for failover so we don't immediately evict everything when nodes reboot.
Tiffany: Let's also update runbooks: how to flip `redwood.io/scale-fallback` annotation per namespace, and how to escalate if hosted-pool utilization spikes.
Alex W: Timeline? Maria, Jamal — can you have the network fix + webhook PoC by EOD PDT? We'll communicate to support and customers about potential disruptions.
Maria S: EOD for webhook PoC seems tight but I'll aim for a stub that adds `nodeAffinity` for tenant namespaces.
Jamal R: I'll handle CA config PR today and run a canary in staging.
Priya: I'll prepare alerts and runbook updates.
Tiffany: I'll coordinate with Security on netpol changes and confirm ops-bot results.
Alex W: Thanks — keep this thread updated with PR links and canary results. :thumbsup:
Maria S: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-configs/pull/821 (WIP)
Jamal R: CA PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-autoscaler-configs/pull/59 (tests green in staging)
